title: Yudan Beribi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In [Kiddushin 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.21b.7), Rabbi Elazar says, “Yudan Beribi used to expound.” (Rashi explains that Yudan was his name and he was a great man of his generation.) Bekhorot 36b cites: “The rabbis taught—R' Yudan said: Berabi used to expound: When they pierce,” etc., “and the Sages say,” etc. This wording suggests that R' Yudan said that Beribi used to expound. The source, however, is Sifrei, Reeh, on “You shall take the awl,” where it reads: “R' Elazar said: Yudan Beribi used to expound.” If so, he is R' Elazar ben Shammua.[^1]

notes.text: Hyman’s Bekhorot wording is ת״ר — א״ר, יודן ברבי היה דורש. The English preserves “said” and reads Yudan as the speaker, following Hyman’s immediately stated interpretation; it does not invent an unnamed additional rabbi or a manuscript lacuna. The Elazar/Yudan quotation is retained separately. בריבי and ברבי remain Beribi and Berabi. The final conditional identification is Hyman’s “If so”; its pronoun is not converted into a new identity binding. The verse is Hyman’s Sifrei locator, without an invented modern section. כא: and לו: conventionally give 21b and 36b.

The William Davidson Hebrew paragraph at Kiddushin 21b:7 explicitly titles Elazar as Rabbi in the corresponding awl teaching. That evidence supports this occurrence alone. Hyman’s differently parsed Bekhorot report, his Sifrei quotation and his final conjectural identification retain R' where their titles are abbreviated. The bounded retrieval of currently numbered Bekhorot 36b did not locate this quotation; its printed locator is retained without claiming a match or substituting another folio. The Sifrei title and Rashi gloss were not independently checked.
